findings.statement: The strongest evidence-respecting admission case is C-PETROV, but it cannot satisfy G-EXT-FEASIBILITY on the current bytes. The exact same-space no-go does not apply to a genuinely distinct conservative test space. The allowed results give a constructive two-node pairing whose determinant a1*a2*p_star*(xi1-xi2)^2 is positive for positive weights, p_star>0, and distinct nodes; they also show that a p test times a terminal-vanishing trial can remain bounded and that a uniform thermal occupation envelope can make the compactified scalar endpoint moments finite. These facts defeat an overbroad universal Petrov rejection. They remain local or conditional facts, not the required complete candidate: no supplied artifact fixes all trial/test spaces, norms, state/cell domain, mass map, process branches, or operation order; proves a uniform inf-sup lower bound; derives the nonsymmetric discrete fermionic entropy inequality; closes the process-total finite-m_e shell and one full-half-line tail; proves deterministic Jacobian/permutation covariance and B3-v2 non-isomorphism; or supplies the binary64 and cost/deflation certificates.

With bounded terminal perturbations it also supplies a plausible single-representation thermal-tail envelope. The overbroad contrary claim that every enrichment is merely B3 or a duplicate tail oracle is unsupported. findings.statement: The local conditioning evidence is exact but cannot certify either candidate uniformly. The frozen two-node matrix is well inside the 1e6 cap, while exact coalescing-node and vanishing-density families make the condition number diverge. Those families decisively falsify the inference that positive weights, positive densities, distinct nodes, or one favorable matrix imply a uniform bound. They do not prove a universal no-go for a future prospectively closed domain with minimum node separation, density lower bounds, scaled norms, and all branch constraints. Wolfram's claim-level fail and SymPy's inconclusive label therefore reflect different treatment of missing evidence; the contract says a theorem gap is INCONCLUSIVE, so this adjudication adopts INCONCLUSIVE while retaining conditioning as a binding non-admission reason.

debate_protocol.self_discover: Extracted only the frozen candidate obligations and the claim-keyed evidence in the three assignment-authorized sibling results. No other result, repository evidence, or scientific computation was used.
debate_protocol.step_back: Separated three levels that the raw labels can conflate: exact rejection of the same-space wording, logical possibility of a materially new Petrov or analytic construction, and present satisfaction of every G-EXT-FEASIBILITY obligation.
metacognitive_self_ask: Am I applying NC-SAME-SPACE outside its finite terminal-vanishing same-space hypotheses?
Am I promoting a positive local determinant, one entropy vector, or scalar tail bound to a uniform candidate theorem?
Am I treating an absent theorem as a universal impossibility rather than INCONCLUSIVE?
Am I ranking non-passing candidates despite the frozen ranking rule?
CoVe: All three allowed results agree that NC-SAME-SPACE does not reject a genuinely distinct Petrov space or analytic enrichment.
Wolfram, Lean, and SymPy agree that the exact local determinant is constructive but not a uniform inf-sup theorem.
Lean and SymPy pass only the scalar entropy subclaim; Wolfram and both other results leave the candidate-wide entropy theorem absent.
Wolfram and SymPy agree that compactified tail plausibility is conditional and not a channel-complete one-consumer tail theorem.
The only verdict-label conflict is conditioning fail versus inconclusive; the underlying facts agree and the contract's theorem-gap rule resolves it to INCONCLUSIVE.
debate_protocol.adversarial_self_ask: Could the strongest candidate be admitted now if every exact positive subclaim were combined? No. Combining local nonsingularity, scalar entropy sign, and conditional tail integrability still leaves the candidate spaces/domain, uniform stability, process-total shell, candidate entropy, one tail consumer, deterministic derivatives/permutations, B3 non-isomorphism, binary64 bound, and both cost obligations undefined or unproved.
debate_protocol.CCoT: NC-SAME-SPACE PASS removes only the same-space PCR-DG wording. C-PETROV is the strongest current steelman because it has an exact constructive local mass pairing; C-ANALYTIC remains a genuine but less specified escape. For each, at least one binding theorem and several structural and numerical preconditions are absent. Under the frozen pass rule no candidate passes, so G-EXT-FEASIBILITY fails on the current bytes without proving either candidate universally impossible.
debate_protocol.PDR: Reject current admission, preserve both candidates only as theorem-incomplete possibilities, preserve STOP/PRESERVE, and do not create PR-01 or claim implementation authority.
debate_protocol.strongest_case_for_admission: C-PETROV: distinct spaces evade the no-go; an exact positive two-node determinant demonstrates local algebraic viability; the p-test/trial product and thermal occupation envelope show compactified integrability is not intrinsically impossible. This is the strongest available construction, but it is not a complete gate artifact.
debate_protocol.strongest_case_against_admission: The gate is conjunctive and candidate-wide. Neither candidate has a fully specified representation/domain, candidate entropy and conservation theorem, process-total shell, single full-tail ownership, deterministic Jacobian/permutation contract, exact B3 non-isomorphism, uniform conditioning proof, binary64 certificate, or cost/deflation plan. Local exact subclaims cannot substitute for those obligations.
